instruction: Decompress the extension file on /home/user/Desktop/ to the same location and install it in Chrome using the unpacked extension option.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

metadata.explanation: Variation with different instruction wording. Task requires extracting the helloExtension.zip file and loading it as an unpacked extension in Chrome. The evaluator uses the existing get_find_unpacked_extension_path getter to retrieve all loaded extension paths from Chrome preferences, then checks if /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension is in the list using the is_in_list metric. No custom functions needed - reuses existing Chrome evaluator infrastructure.
metadata.verification: Verified evaluator logic: get_find_unpacked_extension_path reads Chrome preferences file and extracts all extension paths, is_in_list checks if expected path is in the result list.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: get_find_unpacked_extension_path reads Chrome Preferences file and extracts all loaded extension paths from extensions.settings.<id>.path
Metric logic is correct: is_in_list checks if the expected path exists in the result list using simple membership check
Expected value is correct: /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension matches the extracted directory path from setup config
Complete coverage: The evaluator verifies the critical requirement - that the extension has been loaded as an unpacked extension in Chrome (extraction is a prerequisite)
No runtime issues expected: Chrome Preferences file is accessible post-execution, metric performs simple list membership check
Data flow is semantically correct: getter extracts list of paths → metric checks membership → expected value matches setup
